The two components, MV side load and LV side voltage source, are defined in OpenDSS with some random load value at first. Then, the actual MV side load value for every timestamp is adjusted through Python. The following steps are executed for the power flow simulation with SST using Python [1]: 1. First, solve the system snapshot with a random value for the SST load. 2. Measure the total power supplied by the LV side voltage source. 3. Calculate the power demand on the MV network by adding the SST losses. 4. Update the MV side load kW with the power calculated in 3. 5. Solve the system with updated values. 6. Check MV side voltage if there is any voltage violation. 7. If yes, then increase/decrease the reactive power on the MV side load by a fixed step-size to perform reactive power control. Check and keep on updating the reactive power until the violation is mitigated or until the SST limit is reached. Get the final solution. 8. If not, then move to another timestep. This process is repeated every time step power flow solution. SST reactive power control Reactive power control functionality at the MV terminal is enabled through either one of the two criteria. 1. Volt/var approach – enables reactive power support when the local voltage is beyond the defined voltage range. 2. Relative voltage sensitivity – compares present voltage to previous timestep voltage and absorbs/injects reactive power in case the difference is greater than given threshold. An incremental approach with fixed step change of reactive power is considered to determine the reactive power injection/absorption. Task 2 Develop use case scenarios: In this task, NREL team will generate a set of EV penetration scenarios to simulate the EV charging behavior and estimate charging load profiles and charging requirements. These scenarios will be realistic considering the current and future EV penetration trends, EV infrastructure requirements, and traffic patterns. Further, the increasing penetrations of other DERs such as PV introduce generation variabilities, leading to various operational issues specified above which can be mitigated through the effective use of BESS. High (50-80%) DER penetration scenarios including PV and BESS will be developed by NREL team in this task to study the system level impacts of high DER. The metrics useful for quantifying the value for a distribution system employing the SSTs will be developed by NREL team.
